summary: Aiken County fire tower run by the South Carolina Forestry Commission, with towermen recorded from 1935 to 1939; listed as removed, with no date given.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the eastern U.S. lookouts site; no removal date found.

events.note: Charles F. Powell elected to take charge of the tower from December 1; his family was to move to the tower next week (report dated Nov 22, 1935).
Lightning strike spotted from the tower by towerman W.W. New; fire brought under control promptly.
Leroy Hutchinson named towerman in place of Mr. New, who was appointed county fire warden.

evidence.supports: Agency is the South Carolina Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: South Carolina - Aiken County - South Carolina Forestry Commission

evidence.supports: Nov 22, 1935: Charles F. Powell elected to take charge of the tower from December 1
evidence.quote: Charles F. Powell, of Aiken has been elected to take charge of the Graniteville Fire Tower, and will assume his duties as of December 1st.

evidence.supports: Powell family to move to the tower next week (Nov 22, 1935 report)
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. Powell and family will move to the tower next week.

evidence.supports: Aiken Standard report dated March 31, 1936 (quoted on the Monetta page)
Graniteville tower named among towers already in place, with Wagener, Oskwood and Silverton
evidence.quote: similar towers now located at Wagener, Graniteville, Oskwood and Silverton.

evidence.supports: Aug 9, 1939: towerman W.W. New located a lightning strike from the tower
evidence.quote: W.W. New, towerman at the Graniteville located the lightning strike from his tower.

evidence.supports: The fire was brought under control promptly
evidence.quote: The fire was brought promptly under control.

evidence.supports: Oct 18, 1939: Willie New, formerly the Graniteville towerman, appointed county fire warden
evidence.quote: Willie New, formerly Towerman at Graniteville Tower, has been appointed County Fire Warden

evidence.supports: Oct 18, 1939: Leroy Hutchinson, a native of the Talatha section, appointed towerman to replace Mr. New
evidence.quote: Leroy Hutchinson, a native of the Talatha section of Aiken County, has been appointed Towerman at the Graniteville Fire Tower to replace Mr. New.

evidence.supports: Eastern lookouts record marks the tower as removed
The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: No source gives the build date or design, so the story starts at the first record (Nov 22, 1935 report). The 1936 mention comes from the Monetta page, which quotes an Aiken Standard article dated March 31, 1936. The August 1939 towerman is W.W. New and the October 1939 former towerman is Willie New; the match is by surname and role, and no source says they are the same man outright. The story does not state that they are the same man. The removal date is unknown. No source describes the site today. Two search results (anyplaceamerica.com and aboutus.com) list a Graniteville Fire Tower point near the record coordinates; they were snippets only, not read, and are not used. Access and visit details are unknown and left out of facts.
